editorial_note: Ten original authored questions; source, key and distractor semantics checked against final Chapter 7 after Day 35 navigation. Technical checks do not constitute independent human approval or translation release. The site generates the fifth uncertainty choice and ten-second timing.

questions.prompt: C20 validates the scheduler/API request-ID relationship for q-144. Which new conclusion is supported?

options.text: A named human intentionally registered the task.
The recorded sync-override run issued the S42 edit.
Session s-77 registered sync-override.
The self-reported batch-17 tag now proves approved-job origin.

questions.explanation: B uses C20's preserved run, validated request semantics, C05 request and C13 state relationship to support the specific mechanism. A and C require actor or registration/session evidence not supplied. D contradicts the bounded C14 manifest exclusion and treats a self-reported tag as trusted origin. Mechanism confidence can rise while human attribution stays unknown.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 31, #week-07-day-01, C20 chain and worked graph contrast; §§7.1/7.2; EX031.

questions.prompt: At 09:54, C23 finds neither configuration change in its authoritative approval comparisons. Which classification follows?

options.text: A single attacker made both changes.
Both changes were deliberately malicious.
Every possible inventory has been searched completely.
The supplied owner comparisons classify both changes as unapproved.

questions.explanation: D preserves the approval-source scope and checkpoint. A invents a shared actor; B substitutes malicious intent for an unapproved-change finding; C enlarges selected authoritative comparisons into universal coverage. The 08:47 and 08:52 times do not independently connect the initiators. Inventory deviation, mechanism and intent remain separate claims.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 32, #week-07-day-02, C22/C23 release and classification paragraphs; §7.7; EX032.

questions.prompt: Which source does C22 supply for the 08:52 recovery-method addition?

options.text: A separately retained configuration-audit source with a blank actor field.
A reconstructed copy of C08 detailed sign-in events after their expiry.
A validated human registration identity from s-77.
A functional test proving the recovery method can still authenticate.

questions.explanation: A identifies the supplied producer and its limit. B conflates different sources, retention and fields. C invents attribution from a blank actor. D turns an addition record into a functioning-access test, which remains pending. Its potential access significance warrants an identity-owner contract, not an assertion that every identity path is compromised or fixed.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 32, #week-07-day-02, C22 release and identity-contract row; §7.2 C22; EX032.

questions.prompt: At the 09:54 contract checkpoint, what is the correct state of task disablement and recovery-method remediation?

options.text: Both are completed because the changes are unapproved.
The hold extension authorizes both operations automatically.
Both remain proposed eradication operations with separate authority and checks.
Neither workstream needs baseline preservation because actor identity is unknown.

questions.explanation: C distinguishes the proposed task and identity contracts from C21's already approved/reported hold extension. A invents execution from classification. B borrows a different action's authority. D would discard configuration and run/audit evidence needed to assess the mechanism. Preserve bounded source material, obtain action-specific decisions and keep missing results pending.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 32, #week-07-day-02, two-contract table and worked contrast; §§7.3/7.9; EX032.

questions.prompt: What does C21 add to the initial C17 hold authority?

options.text: Permission to disable all uses of svc-enroll.
A new S42-only extension approval to 10:07 and a distinct operator receipt.
Proof that every write route was blocked continuously.
An unlimited extension until the actor is identified.

questions.explanation: B captures the separate 09:46:30 owner/incident-lead decision and 09:46:45 g-23 report, with a 10:06 review and 10:07 expiry. A changes the target. C promotes permission/report to continuous effect despite limited route evidence. D erases the fixed boundary. Neither C16 tolerance nor C20 mechanism evidence supplies this renewal automatically.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 33, #week-07-day-03, authority table and worked interval example; §7.2 C21; EX033.

questions.prompt: Which operation does C24 actually authorize at 09:59 after preservation?

options.text: Disable only sync-override.
Disable the shared svc-enroll account.
Remove every identity recovery method.
Delete all task evidence and restore business data.

questions.explanation: A names the scoped task-only decision; C24 later reports disablement at 10:03 with an agreeing read-only status. B broadens the action to a legitimate shared dependency. C invents identity remediation. D both destroys the preserved baseline and adds an unauthorized data action. The task result does not prove all access paths removed.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 33, #week-07-day-03, chronological C24 release and authority table; §7.4; EX033.

questions.prompt: No further task run is observed from 10:03 through 10:07. What is needed before calling that a recurrence-test pass?

options.text: Only the task name containing override.
An assumption that four quiet minutes cover every schedule.
A human attribution statement.
A known scheduled opportunity and credible observation coverage.

questions.explanation: D makes absence discriminating: expected trigger metadata and source health/scope are needed to test whether the task would have run. A is a label, B invents the schedule denominator and C answers another question. C24 supports immediate disabled status and a short quiet window, not durable nonexecution, all-runner coverage or legitimate-job success.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 33, #week-07-day-03, worked interval example; Day 34, #week-07-day-04, C7X recurrence gate; EX033/EX034.

questions.prompt: In a separate §7.11 run, observed batch-17 is removed. What happens to the two original printed forward differences?

options.text: They now print batch-17 as a missing approved task.
Both printed lists become empty.
They remain unchanged; a reverse key difference is needed to reveal the missing task.
They prove sync-override was installed by an attacker.

questions.explanation: C follows the actual program: observed-minus-approved still names sync-override, and the request-union difference still names q-144. A asks the forward calculation to produce its reverse. B ignores the retained unexpected task/request. D invents intent from finite sets. The reverse key difference would identify missing batch-17 in the supplied map, without proving whether the job vanished or collection was incomplete.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 34, #week-07-day-04, worked transcripts and W7-RELATION direction control; corrected §7.11 failure injection; EX034.

questions.prompt: In C7X, all other BASE flags stay unchanged but expected_fire is False. Which verdict is correct?

options.text: NO_EXPECTED_TRIGGER_TESTED.
BOUNDED_SCHEDULER_CHECK_NOT_ERADICATION.
Proof that all persistence was removed.
Proof that the legitimate batch failed.

questions.explanation: A is the exact refusal to treat no invocation opportunity as a successful recurrence test. B requires the declared opportunity gate to pass. C exceeds even BASE's bounded verdict. D invents a service failure from a different input. The function trusts supplied flags and reports its first blocker; it does not authenticate a schedule or real observations.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 34, #week-07-day-04, C7X recurrence gate and adverse interpretation; §7.14 NO_TRIGGER_ELAPSED row; EX034.

questions.prompt: At 10:07, which handoff respects C24 and the hold-expiry decision?

options.text: All access is revoked and eradication is complete.
The S42 hold continues indefinitely under C17.
Task-specific improvement is observed; identity, recurrence and service checks remain pending under monitoring.
The unknown actor means no technical mechanism has been established.

questions.explanation: C preserves C24's task report/short observations, C22's unresolved identity concern, pending scheduled/service coverage and the owner's 10:06 no-renewal decision with monitoring/escalation. A invents universal remediation. B overrides the C21 fixed 10:07 boundary. D discards the validated C20 mechanism merely because human attribution is unknown. No later result belongs in this handoff.
questions.source: Chapter 7, Week 7 / course Day 35, #week-07-day-05, worked evidence package and model handoff; §§7.10/7.15; EX035.
